teams.heading: Fiji's Koli Sewabu says FRU will follow Mark Nawaqanitawase's possible switch
teams.body: FRU chief executive Koli Sewabu says Fiji are following Mark Nawaqanitawase's possible switch of allegiance with interest, after the winger's agent said he was weighing up a move ahead of his return to union. The 11-cap Wallabies winger is eligible for Fiji, Italy and Australia. Wallabies coach Les Kiss, meanwhile, says: "I'll wait until the end of the year to see where he sits."

lead.why: The open Nawaqanitawase storyline has the freshest Fiji-side reaction, from the FRU chief executive.

teams.heading: Former England lock David Ribbans set to become Springbok-eligible on 27 October
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has confirmed his interest in David Ribbans, the former England lock who becomes eligible to represent South Africa on 27 October. Ribbans, born in Somerset West and now at Toulon, completes a three-year stand-down period under World Rugby's amended rules, which allow a player who qualifies through birth, citizenship or ancestry to switch. Erasmus said: "We are also looking at someone like David Ribbans, not that they must get their hopes up." Eligibility does not guarantee a switch, and Ribbans has previously said that changing allegiance would not be right towards England.

lead.why: A new men's national-side story about a former England lock's eligibility for South Africa, with a direct England angle.

teams.heading: Louis Bielle-Biarrey stranded at Bristol Airport before Bordeaux Bègles' Gloucester opener
teams.body: Bordeaux Bègles had four players held at Bristol Airport ahead of their Investec Champions Cup opener against Gloucester, France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey among them. Loose forward Romain Gardrat, loosehead Matis Perchaud and Tonga's Toma Taufa were also stranded with a fitness coach, a club source told AFP, because their Electronic Travel Authorisations were linked to renewed passports and no new permits had been obtained. The club contacted the French embassy in London, and the issue was eventually resolved, allowing the players to rejoin their teammates.

lead.why: The Flament injury is already covered in today's edition, so this is the strongest fresh France-linked item, and it is clearly labelled as a Bordeaux Bègles club story.

teams.heading: Sam Prendergast scores 14 as Leinster beat Clermont 48-23 in Champions Cup
teams.body: Sam Prendergast scored 14 points and was named Player of the Match for a second successive game as Leinster came from behind twice to beat Clermont 48-23 in Pool 1 of the Champions Cup. The Ireland fly-half turned a 15-16 half-time deficit into a win, and his best moment came two minutes after half-time, when he burst out of defence and kicked for Jimmy O'Brien on the left touchline. Prendergast had lost the No.10 jersey to Jack Crowley midway through the Six Nations.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 to South Africa at home in November 2025
teams.body: The last meeting between the sides was a 32-14 home defeat for Italy in November 2025, an International Friendly. The two sides meet again in Round four of the Nations Championship, Italy's next fixture. Italy come into it 11th of 12 in the log after three defeats, most recently a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round three.

teams.heading: Women's rugby: Desiree Miller reaches 20 Test tries in Scotland's 56-12 defeat
teams.body: Desiree Miller became the first Wallaroo to score 20 women's Test tries in Australia's 56-12 win over Scotland at Accor Stadium in Sydney on Saturday. Shifted to full-back, the speedster scored from near-identical plays off scrums as Australia piled up 42 consecutive points. Amelia Whitaker scored her maiden try for the Wallaroos, and Scotland's tries came from Katie Buchanan and captain Rachel Malcolm.

lead.why: It is the NEW item, it gives the day a different angle from the already-run defeat story, and it is a women's story labelled as one.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards signs Argentina contract running until after 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Shaun Edwards' move to Argentina is now a signed deal, with Sky Sports reporting his contract with Los Pumas runs until after the 2027 Rugby World Cup. He joins as defence coach, and reports say the move rules out a role under Steve Borthwick. Ruck has also reported that Edwards will not coach England at the 2027 World Cup.

teams.heading: Les Kiss calls Wallabies' first half 'not acceptable' after Bledisloe loss
teams.body: Les Kiss was scathing about the first half of Saturday's second Bledisloe Test, a 43-21 defeat in Sydney. "It's just not acceptable what was put out there," the Wallabies coach said, after the All Blacks claimed a 13th straight Bledisloe win. The Guardian called it a second thrashing in a week, with errors and execution failures aiding the visitors. Two second-half tries, from Tom Wright and Filipo Daugunu, thinned the margin slightly.

lead.why: A fresh coach reaction to Saturday's 43-21 Bledisloe defeat, and the strongest men's national-side item in the pack.

teams.heading: Japan's biggest win in 11 games: 63-14 over USA in September
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Japan have scored 309 points and conceded 308, an average of 28.1 points scored and 28 conceded per game. The biggest win in that window was a 63-14 victory over USA at home in September, in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. Japan scored 63 points in that game alone, against 14 conceded.

teams.heading: All Blacks down Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney for 13th straight win
teams.body: The All Blacks ran in seven tries to Australia's three on Saturday, beating the Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney for their 13th straight win over their trans-Tasman rivals. It follows a 50-19 win at Eden Park that saw New Zealand retain the Bledisloe Cup for the 24th consecutive year. The result has moved the All Blacks to 92.27 rating points, 0.82 behind the Springboks at the top of the World Rugby rankings.

lead.why: A new national result, confirmed by the rankings report, and the strongest fresh item not already covered on this tab.

teams.heading: Cheswill Jooste hat-trick sends Bulls past Stade Français in Champions Cup opener
teams.body: Cheswill Jooste scored a hat-trick as the Bulls beat Stade Français 56-20 in Saturday's Investec Champions Cup opener, crossing inside half a minute and again in the 73rd minute. The 20-year-old wing's treble was one of eight Bulls tries; Cobus Wiese, Cameron Hanekom, Marco van Staden, Jeandre Rudolph and Jan-Hendrik Wessels also scored, and Handré Pollard converted every one. Jacques Botha and Petero Mailulu scored Stade's tries.

lead.why: A 20-year-old Bulls wing's hat-trick in a 56-20 Champions Cup win is the story a fan would text a mate, and it is the strongest new item on the shortlist that isn't already covered.
